chunks: A number of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Husayn ibn Kharijah, from Muyassir ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not form contracts/deal with people who have a chronic ailment/disability, for they are the most unjust of things.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dealing with people who have chronic diseases according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises against commercial or social dealings with those suffering from 'Aah' (chronic ailment or disability), characterizing them as 'the most unjust' (azlam shay'). While 'Aah' can refer to physical or mental conditions, Shia scholars often interpret this as a practical caution regarding their potential for heightened emotional volatility or tendency to transfer their discomfort to others, rather than a definitive judgment of their moral character.
